subject: general
question: Which of the following sectors is second largest employment generator in India after agriculture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Textiles Sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **textiles sector** is the second-largest employment generator in India after agriculture.
 
• It employs over 45 million people directly and around 60 million people indirectly in India.
 
• The sector includes a wide range of activities such as** cotton, jute, silk, wool, and man-made fibers production.**
 
• India is one of the largest producers and exporters of textiles and garments in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Textile Industry in India**

 
 
• It contributes **approximately 2.3% to India's GDP.**
 
• The industry contributes 7% to the industrial output and 12% to the country's export earnings.
 
• India's textile industry is a significant contributor to the national economy and plays a crucial role in its socio-economic development.
 
• The industry is characterized by the presence of small-scale, medium-sized, and large enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**
 
 
• The government has launched various schemes like the **Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS)** and the **Scheme for Integrated Textile Parks (SITP).**
 
• These initiatives aim to support the modernization and development of the textile sector.
 
• The government also promotes handloom products under the "India Handloom" brand.
 
 
 
• **Challenges and Opportunities**
 
 
• The sector faces challenges such as outdated technology, a lack of skilled labor, and competition from other countries.
 
• However, there are opportunities for growth with the rising demand for textiles domestically and internationally.
 
• Investments in technology and skill development can enhance the sector's productivity and competitiveness.
